$comment: The 24,000-character window cut, read against the arm that differs in exactly one field, on the population `report.ts` says to read. Two corrections are folded into this version and both are recorded rather than applied silently: the control (was `42355323615`, which moves `ask` alongside the window) and the accuracy population (was `feature.metrics`, the first repetition, where `ablation.featureAggregate.avg` is the mean over all of them).

ratio.measure: median promptChars of the reduced arm / median promptChars of the control arm, same 500 questions, same reader, same judge

accuracyTwoVariableControl.label: two variables: maxPromptChars AND ask; not attributable to the window

corrections.why: it moves `ask` in the same dispatch that shrank the room, so the deltas belong to the pair. Against the one-field control the cut is smaller on every capability except TR.

`report.ts` states that `featureAggregate.avg` is the right population because every cost ratio denominator must describe the same repetitions as the numerator. The first repetition of `42310779222` is 90.20% against a four-repetition mean of 90.85%; of `42355323615` 91.40% against 91.95%.

verdict.C3: unrun: the reduced arm ran 2 repetitions against 4, so the bill is not admissible as evidence
verdict.accuracyCost: overall -2.65, TR -4.53; the margin rule blocks both, IE -2.33 and MR -2.27 sit inside it, and no paired test certifies anything (TR 0 won / 5 lost, p = 0.0625)

note: The room ratio is robust to the control choice (0.4874 against the one-field arm, 0.4864 against the two-variable one), because the room is a configuration constant. The accuracy attribution is not robust to it, and that is the whole of the first correction.
